transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-03 09:30 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Noah Kim, Ava Patel, Liam Chen, Sofia Martinez, Priya Singh, Ben Lewis; and internal stakeholders Elena Ortiz, Marcus Boyd, Zara Hughes.

Summary: quick sync on token/unit economics for Q4 roadmap, align on incident-prep for upcoming private deployment pilot, and decide short list of launch safety net items.

[00:00] Noah Kim: okay, cool, let's get started. thanks everyone for jumping on. goal for today is to lock down the token-econ changes we want in the roadmap, and to make decisions on the incident prep checklist for the private pilot.
[00:28] Ava Patel: I put a short deck in the calendar invite but i also added the draft spreadsheet, so if folks only have their phones you can still look later. main constraints: we have a target to reduce per-token cost 15% on median workloads without increasing 95th percentile latency.
[01:05] Liam Chen: just to call out, the 95th is going to bite us if we shift batching aggressively. we've seen spikes earlier where the KV-cache thrash made tail latency worse.
[01:22] Priya Singh: yeah we measured that — when the cache hit rate falls below about 82% the per-request token time jumps. i have some prototype quantization profiles that shave tokens but alter softmax calibration, so quality regression is a risk.
[01:40] Ben Lewis: hmm, can we do a A/B against our eval set? maybe run the quantized variant only for 10% and measure rouge/emd drift.
[01:53] Ava Patel: that's exactly the proposal — Priya runs the token-cost sim and Ben hooks up the eval suite. Noah, you said you wanted a customer-facing note, too?
[02:12] Noah Kim: yeah, we need a short blurb that explains degradations and what to expect if fallback happens: model variant swap, throttling, or degrade to cached responses. this is for sales and enterprise customers so Legal needs to sign off.
[02:30] Zara Hughes: noted — legal will need to check the wording around "degraded" and claims on availability; also need to confirm KMS/HSM key handling if customers request private deployments with their own keys.
[02:46] Marcus Boyd: speaking of private deployments, we need to rehearse the incident runbook where network flaps in the customer's VPC cause a control-plane split. how does the agent-side fallback behave?
[03:05] Sofia Martinez: current design: agent will switch to local-only mode and route inference to on-prem queue, but we lack good telemetry on that handoff. i want hooks to emit event traces when KV cache warms or is evicted so SRE can diagnose.
[03:26] Liam Chen: okay, add that to the engineering checklist — instrument eviction counts and pre/post-eviction latencies. Priya can you add the metrics to the canary?
[03:40] Priya Singh: yes. i'll add histograms for kv_eviction_count, kv_warm_time, and request_latency_post_warm.
[03:55] [small crosstalk — someone drops a file]
[04:10] Ava Patel: on the token-econ side: we proposed three knobs: batching window cap, quantization profile (8-bit / 4-bit mixed), and prefix caching TTLs. which of these are highest impact with lowest user-visible risk?
[04:35] Ben Lewis: prefix TTLs are low risk; they just increase cache hit rate for common prompts. quantization is high reward but highest risk for hallucination. batching window cap reduces cost but increases tail.
[04:55] Noah Kim: so priority: prefix caching tweaks first, then a controlled quant experiment behind canary, and use batching as a fallback knob.
[05:10] Sofia Martinez: agree. also, we need to make sure tracing has correlation ids for requests that hit the cache vs not — otherwise it's hard to correlate the latency anomalies.
[05:28] Liam Chen: i want to call out a previous incident where evictions were mis-attributed to autoscaler churn — memory got tight because we pinned too many KV shards per GPU. we need a rollout guard to cap KV shards per node during canary.
[05:50] Priya Singh: noted — cap shards to X during staged rollout. i'll put the exact number in the sim.
[06:05] [07:12] Ben Lewis: quick note — competitor HyperscaleX published a paper about dynamic batching that used sequence-length bucketing to reduce wasted tokens. worth testing but probably post Q4.
[06:30] Ava Patel: legal question — Zara, SOC2: does running canary on actual customer PII-level prompts require any extra steps?
[06:48] Zara Hughes: yes, if the test data is PII we need a separate data handling plan and potentially an agreement amendment. otherwise use synthetic or scrubbed datasets. also confirm audit log retention for private pilots; some customers require 7 years — that affects storage cost.
[07:12] Noah Kim: good to note. We'll keep canaries on synthetic/scrubbed content unless customers opt in.
[07:30] [08:00] Sofia Martinez: incident playbook action: we define the rollback thresholds. proposal: if 95th latency increases >30% for two consecutive 5-minute windows, or error rate increases by 0.5% absolute, trigger automatic rollback. any objections?
[07:55] Liam Chen: that seems reasonable but 0.5% might be noisy at low volume; maybe use relative increase and require sustained >2x baseline for at least 10 minutes for low-volume endpoints.
[08:20] Priya Singh: also add model-quality guardrails from Ben's evals: if our eval metric delta exceeds defined threshold (we'll set per-model), auto disable quantized variant.
[08:38] Ben Lewis: yes i'll draft thresholds — will share in the eval PR.
[08:50] Ava Patel: for customer communication we need two artifacts: a short FAQ and a deeper runbook. Noah will own the FAQ, Sofia will own the runbook. Noah?
[09:02] Noah Kim: i'll draft the FAQ and coordinate with Marketing for tone. Sofia will own technical runbook and ensure it's linked in engineering playbooks.
[09:20] [10:00] Marcus Boyd: one more infra ask — can we limit the number of model swaps per minute? we had cascading thrash when many requests hit fallback concurrently. some rate-limiter at the routing layer would smooth the churn.
[09:50] Sofia Martinez: yes implement a soft rate limiter for model variant swaps with a token bucket and warm-up window. we'll also add jitter to prevent thundering herd.
[10:15] Liam Chen: sounds good. also add an emergency circuit-breaker that prevents new canary traffic if memory pressure > 85% cluster-wide.
[10:30] Priya Singh: on the economics sim, i'm modelling the cost difference with three scenarios: optimistic cache retention, median, and pessimal. optimistic shows 20% cost savings with prefix tweaks + 4-bit quant, median shows 8–12%, pessimal 0–3% with spike in tail.
[10:55] Ben Lewis: can you surface the token-per-second assumptions and the sample prompt distribution? we need to make sure the eval set matches real prompts not marketing demos.
[11:10] Priya Singh: yes will include request-size histograms and a small sample of prompt buckets.
[11:25] [12:00] Ava Patel: timeline check: Q4 roadmap milestone is to have the private pilot feature-complete and have two enterprise customers on reserved capacity by the end of October. that gives us roughly 8 weeks. are the action items feasible?
[11:45] Liam Chen: from infra perspective yes if we prioritize the instrumentation and shard caps now. the kernel selection changes for quant might slip into late October but we can ship quant as opt-in.
[12:05] Noah Kim: prioritize safety features first — rate limiter, canary soak, eviction metrics, audit log decisions. quant as opt-in after we have guardrails.
[12:20] [13:00] Zara Hughes: note on compliance — for customers demanding specific data residency, private deploys must have audit entries tagged with region/source; Legal will need a short appendix in the contract.
[12:45] Marcus Boyd: operational note — prepare a two-hour warroom drill with oncall and SEs before we open pilot. simulate a KV-cache eviction storm and a partial region outage.
[13:05] Sofia Martinez: i'll run the drill — propose 2026-09-20 as a date, invite owners.
[13:20] Priya Singh: for the canary I'll produce a small harness that can flip quant on/off per-request and log evaluation diffs inline.
[13:35] Ben Lewis: ace, that'll give us fine-grained signal.
[13:50] [14:00] Noah Kim: OK let's do a quick recap and owners: Priya — token-cost sim and harness [due 2026-09-10]; Sofia — canary soak and runbook, plus drill on 2026-09-20 [sooner if possible]; Liam — KV shard cap validation and eviction metrics [due 2026-09-09]; Ava — update roadmap doc and coordinate executive sync [due 2026-09-08]; Zara — legal signoff on customer note and KMS guidance [due 2026-09-12]; Noah — customer-facing FAQ draft [due 2026-09-09].
[14:30] Ava Patel: i'll also prepare a one-pager for Sales with the key fallbacks and their expected user impact.
[14:45] [15:00] small pause, background noise (keyboard clack)
[15:15] Liam Chen: one minor technical nit — need to ensure observability tags include model variant id and quant profile name; otherwise we can't trace quality regressions to profile.
[15:30] Priya Singh: yep i'll include profile name in the event payload.
[15:42] Noah Kim: any blockers we're missing?
[15:48] Marcus Boyd: capacity: ensure Dedicated reserved pools have headroom for canary traffic; ops will set aside a small burst pool.
[16:00] Sofia Martinez: and SSO — ensure SAML provisioning is working for pilot customers; can't have onboarding blocked by auth problems.
[16:15] Zara Hughes: i'll flag the contract addendum for SAML/KMS requirements.
[16:30] [17:00] Ben Lewis: one last thing — document how we measure "user-visible impact". i propose two signals: customer-reported incidents and a synthetic SLO delta measured on the eval harness.
[16:55] Noah Kim: good. we'll define those in the FAQ.
[17:10] Ava Patel: ok that's it from me. thanks all.
[17:22] [End 10:32 local?] (meeting ran ~62 minutes)
